messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Query on getting Deducer to plot bar graph
parts:
Bruce,

The plot is not to hard to create in the plot builder. The data needs to be in long format rather than wide:

dat <- structure(list(station = structure(c(1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 1L, 2L, 
1L, 2L), .Label = c("1", "2"), class = "factor"), V2 = structure(c(1L, 
1L, 2L, 2L, 3L, 3L, 4L, 4L), .Label = c("Dicalb", "Perkap", "Permac", 
"Sacbil"), class = "factor"), V3 = c(0.01, 0.03, 2.58, 0.78, 
0.7, 0.78, 4.29, 27.07)), row.names = c(NA, -8L), .Names = c("station", 
"V2", "V3"), class = "data.frame")

the generated ggplot2 code is:

ggplot() +
geom_bar(aes(y = V3,x = V2,fill = station),data=dat,position = position_dodge())

I've attached the plot as a  .ggp file which can be opened with the Open Plot menu item. I've also included a template.



Best,
Ian

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Query on getting Deducer to plot bar graph
parts:
Without your data, it is difficult to say. You want your data to have two or three columns. one for the x, one for the fill and (optionally) one for the y. Go to Geometric Elements and select bar. In The dialog put the x- variable into the "x" slot. Toggle the fill slot so that you can drop a variable in there and do so. If you want your y-axis to represent something other than the counts of the observations, drop the variable you want to represent in there.


ian
